claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2022-12-09 reports: In Gushegu, the author links heat stress and resource scarcity to herders’ mobility and feeding adaptations that damage crops or breach tree tenure and can trigger farmer-herder disputes.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2022-12-09 reports: A Gushegu chief-led committee hears farmer-herder disputes and may decide compensation, but is informal and cannot enforce decisions; some parties distrust its decisions or allege favoritism.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Interview-based local institutional description; allegations of favoritism are respondents’ perceptions, not adjudicated misconduct or evidence of effective mediation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat stress and changing availability of water and fodder.
pathways.documented_impact: Reported changes in herding/feeding practices can lead to crop damage or contested tree use.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Land/tree tenure rules, resource allocation, politicized identities and limited trust/enforcement in dispute institutions.
pathways.possible_consequence: The Gushegu account describes verbal disputes and warns of escalation; climate is an exacerbating factor, not the primary or sufficient cause.
alternative_explanations: Political mobilization, land acquisition, population pressure, crop damage, stigmatization and weak dispute mechanisms independently shape tensions.
pathways.uncertainty: A 2022 case-based brief and interviews, not a climate-attributable conflict estimate or current incident map. Ethnic identity is not treated as a propensity for violence.
resilience_factors: Inclusive, trusted dispute resolution is relevant; committee existence alone is not evidence of enforceable or fair outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: In Gushegu, reported heat-related herding adjustments can encounter crop/tree-tenure disputes within a politically mediated conflict setting; no independent climate effect is estimated.

executive_assessment.text: Kintampo assessment examples distinguish selected-community exposure and adaptive capacity; rankings from nine purposively selected communities cannot be generalized nationwide.
Gushegu adds a conditional heat/resource-pressure mechanism mediated by tenure and dispute institutions; political and identity dynamics remain central.
Regional profiles and warning-system arrangements add capacity detail, without proving effective warning reach or reduced losses.
